propositions: Five test modules rebuild equivalent git/rebar topologies from scratch once per test consumer, contributing 103.416 measured worker-seconds across repeated invariant fixture construction.

Runtime probes measured real-build versus isolated-copy performance ratios of 12x, 17.7x, 23x, 13.8x, and 15.7x, demonstrating that setup dominates test execution time and topology construction can be cached and copied.

The clone_topology_template helper remints .env-id and .signing-key but initially left .opcert-key/.pub copied verbatim, violating the isolation contract that per-test copies cannot share signing keys; this was repaired by discarding copied private keys and using lazy first-use generation.

Behavioral sentinels validate isolation contracts covering half-rewritten pointers, bare worktrees, source-path leakage, shared refs/object stores, identity/signing isolation, virgin templates, and mutable config; mutation testing confirmed RED with defects present and GREEN after repair.

All 125 affected tests passed with no removal, skipping, sampling, xfailing, or weakening of assertions; full default (13,441 tests) and integration (167 tests) selectors passed with all existing coverage preserved.

The five targeted repeated-setup mechanisms were eliminated by switching from function-scoped invariant construction to session-scoped template building plus per-test isolated copies with repair, measured through paired before/after setup timing and disappearance of >1s fixture_setup spans from the affected modules.
